newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent skids, other N.Sea crudes turn corner.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent skids, other N.Sea crudes turn corner.

text.p: North Sea crudes were mixed Friday as Dated Brent hit the skids after this week's main buyer put his cheque-book away and other grades perked up on tighter supply, traders said.

One of the Brent cargoes nominated loading dates on Friday (Nov 10-12) traded at Nov Brent -20 cents, after a sale Thursday at the equivalent of Nov +12. "It should have been here a long time ago," said a trader.
Traders said Shell's buying spree earlier this week (it holds some eight cargoes) kept Dated Brent artificially high, possibly with the aim of benefiting a related swaps position.
Friday saw the first clocking of the week - BP was left with a Nov 9-11 cargo - while the other set of dates, Nov 11-13, were kept and then offered by a Wall Street trader at Nov Brent -20 cents.
Next week's Brent CFDs lost six cents to Dec Brent +2/+7 cents, worth about Nov Brent -30 cents.
Intermonth paper spreads firmed a few cents with Dec Brent which gained 21 cents to $23.96 a barrel by 1730 GMT.
Differentials for other North Sea crudes bottomed and appeared to have turned the corner after a clear out of prompt barrels earlier in the week, traders said.
Deals were scarce but a Nov 22-24 Norwegian Ekofisk traded at Dated Brent +30 cents a barrel, five cents firmer than trade on Wednesday.

Urals in the Mediterranean was under pressure from end month cargoes but Siberian Light was better supported, with a cargo on offer at Dated Brent +50 cents after trade earlier this week at +42 cents.
Traders said Syrian Light for November would probably be settled at Dated Brent -5 cents, an increase of 25 cents over October.
